text:
olivia: Thanks again for joining the all-hands. Quick follow-up: could the kernel + runtime leads spell out the rollout timeline, default batching/caching settings, and any major tradeoffs we should flag to product/SEs? Trying to set expectations for customers and the docs team.

james: Kernel team update — short version: alpha kernels to staging next week, small canary in prod at ~3 weeks, broad rollout week 6 if no regressions. Branch is kernel/opt-1, current alpha commit f3a9b2c.

sofia: For the docs team: will there be behavioral changes (e.g., logits differences) consumers need to watch for or is this purely perf?

james: Good q. Primary goal is perf+mem. We expect tiny numeric diffs due to FP/quantization paths but not meaningful behavioural shifts for prompts we've vetted. We'll provide regression dashboards and an opt-out flag.

kai: Can you share the default batching/caching defaults you plan to ship? Ops needs to update sample configs.

james: Default we'll recommend in 1.0: max_batch_size=64, max_latency_ms=25, dynamic_batching=true. KV prefix cache enabled with default ttl_ms=60000. These are conservative to avoid tail latency spikes. Example config we expect in the release notes:
```yaml
runtime:
  batching:
    max_batch_size: 64
    max_latency_ms: 25
    dynamic_batching: true
  cache:
    prefix_kv: true
    ttl_ms: 60000
  kernel_flags:
    enable_opt_kernels: true
```

ravi: Any quantization caveats? We saw q8 caused small quality regressions on longer contexts last cycle.

james: We're shipping opt kernels that are quantization-friendly, but for models with >8k context and heavy arithmetic (math prompts, code) we recommend `quantization: q4f` only after perf validation. We'll auto-run evals on customers' pinned model snapshots during canary if they opt in.

maria: Who owns the eval suite for the rollout? I can add critical prompt sets for SE/trial customers.

james: Maria — thanks. Can you add the top 10 customer prompt sets to `evals/kernel_opt_1` by Monday? We'll wire the regression alerts to the Optimize dashboard.

noah: Telemetry/observability: we'll emit two new spans: `kernel_sched` and `kv_cache_hit`. Also adding token-level cost breakdown per-request. Heads up: this will increase trace volume ~8%.

olivia: Is the increased trace volume something we should default on for all customers, or opt-in?

noah: Default will be sampling at 10% for hosted by default, 0% for Dedicated/Private unless explicitly enabled. We can bump for SRE when debugging.

sofia: Docs note: add a "What changed" small section plus migration checklist (opt-in flags, how to disable). Also include guidance for Dedicated customers with custom kernels.

james: Tradeoffs summary for leadership & product:
- perf: ~1.8-2.5x throughput for common gen workloads.
- latency: median improves, but tail depends on batch shape and dynamic batching.
- quality: minor numeric diffs; risk with lower-precision quant paths on niche prompts.
- ops: more telemetry, small infra config churn (autoscaler tuning).

deploy-bot: Canary started for service=generator cluster=prod-eu at ts=1834001245 (image: registry.redwood/kernel-opt-1:f3a9b2c) :rocket:

ravi: If the canary shows quality regressions, what's the fallback?

james: Automatic fallback policy: if regression_alert_rate > 0.5% or latency_p95 increases > 20% we rollback to previous kernel variant and open a canary incident. Rollback is automated for hosted.

maria: Action items: 1) docs doc + migration checklist (sofia), 2) add customer prompt sets to evals (maria), 3) telemetry sampling config (noah), 4) canary watch runbook (james). I'll collate and send to product.

olivia: Perfect — thanks. Can everyone briefly react with :thumbsup: when you've acknowledged your action item?

james: :thumbsup:

sofia: :thumbsup: adding notes to the docs backlog (card #RW-2043).

maria: :thumbsup: I'll upload the eval sets by EOD Monday.

noah: :thumbsup: setting sampling knobs now.

ravi: :thumbsup: will monitor quality dashboard.

olivia: I'll follow up with product for customer comms. Thanks all!
